statements.text: AND WHEREAS, Indiana lawmakers’ attempts to censor conversations about LGBTQIA+ and the required “outing” of some LGBTQIA+ students further discriminates against and harasses students based on their gender identity, gender expression, and sexual orientation;
statements.context: Board Resolution 2023-07, fixed text signed by Hennessey as Vice President (scanned PDF, transcribed from image)

statements.text: NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Board continues to declare the Corporation to be a Safe Place for students, meaning that the Corporation is a place for LGBTQIA+ students to learn, thrive, and seek assistance, information, and support.

statements.text: BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Board strongly opposes any Indiana laws or proposed legislation, including 2023 House Bill 1608, that limit the rights of LGBTQIA+ students and put them at greater risk for discrimination or harassment.
statements.context: Board Resolution 2023-07, signed text; HB 1608 = Indiana bill limiting instruction on sexuality and requiring parent notice of name/pronoun requests

statements.text: BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Board hereby directs the Monroe County Community School Corporation (MCCSC) administration to work with members of the LGBTQIA+ community and MCCSC staff to create a policy that prohibits the bullying and/or harassment of LGBTQIA+ individuals in accordance with state and federal law, and with the review and input required by the applicable Collective Bargaining Agreements.

statements.text: "And whereas the Monroe County Community School Corporation has a responsibility to ensure that all students regardless of gender identity, gender expression or sexual orientation can safely attend our schools free of prohibited discrimination."

statements.text: “The court’s decision to strike down the Biden Administration’s Title IX rewrite is a huge victory for the integrity of women’s and girls’ sports. Allowing biological males to compete in women’s sports threatens the very opportunities Title IX was meant to protect. As a mother of daughters, I applaud this ruling and remain committed to ensuring only biological females compete in women’s sports.”
statements.context: statement on federal court vacating the 2024 Title IX rule

statements.text: “We have seen women, strong women like Riley Gaines, speak to the real harm female athletes experience from the issues we are discussing today. For those who do not know, Riley is a former University of Kentucky champion swimmer. My own daughters are swimmers and we have admired Riley’s courage.
statements.context: House floor remarks managing rule debate on H.R. 734 (Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act)

statements.text: “Unfortunately, women are becoming collateral damage. Riley told me stories about her competitor, a biological male, sharing locker rooms and showers with her teammates. And how a year later, one teammate who was quiet at the time wrote letters to her about how the experience still traumatizes her.
statements.context: House floor remarks on H.R. 734

statements.text: “Riley also shared a story of how when that same biological male competitor won, she was asked to step away from the medal ceremony photo. The sport she loved had been reduced to a photo-op. This is not progress, this is quite the opposite,” said Congresswoman Houchin.
statements.context: House floor remarks on H.R. 734

statements.text: “Yet, parents are left pleading. They are left to plead for information, to plead for safety of their kids in public restrooms, to plead for a quality education, and to plead for anyone who would listen to help restore their parental rights,”  Congresswoman Houchin continued.
statements.context: House floor remarks managing rule debate on H.R. 5, Parents Bill of Rights

statements.text: In fact, one father in Virginia had to learn his daughter was assaulted in a high school bathroom from his child, not the school.
statements.context: Fox News op-ed reposted on House site, arguing for H.R. 5

statements.text: Just last month, a New Jersey judge ruled to block multiple school districts from notifying parents of a child’s gender identity change. Stories like these shouldn’t become the new normal.
statements.context: same op-ed; two consecutive one-sentence paragraphs

statements.text: As I said on the floor of the House of Representatives, sending a child to a public school does not terminate the parents’ rights at the door.
statements.context: same op-ed

statements.text: Parents should be in the driver's seat of their children's education. The pandemic opened American parents' eyes to the reality of our public school system, and millions of parents didn't like what they saw.
statements.context: campaign site plank 'PROTECT PARENTAL RIGHTS' (third-person page); not tied to gender explicitly

statements.text: “This issue is personal for me, as a member of the LGBTQ community. It is personal for my family, as I have a transgender younger sister. statements.text: They voted to make our state a place where LGBTQ+ kids don’t feel safe to be themselves.

statements.text: “Assembly Bill 510 is about limiting education on race and our history, including discussing topics like Martin Luther King, Jr. and his work. Under this bill, it is less likely that our kids would learn about his and other civil rights leaders’ legacy – that is a problem. This bill also continues to attack LGBTQ+ kids and their families.

statements.text: “When it comes to AB 305, I wish we would stop playing politics with our kids. I wish we could fund our public schools adequately, as the people of Wisconsin have asked for again and again, without needing to put more public dollars into unaccountable private schools that have limited public oversight and don’t have to serve every child, whether they have a disability or an LGBTQ+ identity.

statements.text: “As out LGBTQ+ legislators, allies, and advocates, we are dedicated to expanding equal rights and protections for all Wisconsinites—especially as Donald Trump and far-right extremists across our country ratchet up the rhetoric and target LGBTQ+ rights.

statements.text: “Although these bills will not become law in our state, their reintroduction alone is harmful and dangerous. statements.text: “When transgender athletes compete against women, women’s sports are no longer women’s sports; they become unisex athletic events,”  Sen. Lee  said. “This bill would protect the opportunity of girls throughout America to athletically compete against other girls.”
statements.context: introducing Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act

statements.text: “Why is the federal bureaucracy in the child mutilation business?” said Senator Mike Lee. “Americans don’t want to pay millions for these disturbing studies where hundreds of kids are experimented on with puberty-blocking drugs. President Trump rightly halted this attack on America’s kids. Our bill will codify his agenda to keep federal dollars out of gender transition research involving minors.”
statements.context: introducing Protecting Our Kids from Harmful Research Act

statements.text: “There are kids in America receiving life-altering gender surgeries before they graduate high school. There are kids being given hormone blockers that can cause bone loss, depression, and myriad other medical issues when they should be playing hopscotch and riding bikes,” said Senator Mike Lee.
statements.context: cosponsoring STOP Act

statements.text: “Our kids deserve safe childhoods and informed consent, but instead they have harmful procedures pushed on them by predatory doctors who won’t have to live with the consequences. I’m proud to cosponsor the STOP Act to outlaw risky gender transition procedures on minors, empower victims to sue for damages, and award the penalty funds from criminal doctors to their victims as recovery compensation.”
statements.context: same release, continuation of Lee quote

statements.text: “Our nation’s capital should not be a refuge for people who take the lives of children or wreck their bodies with illegal drugs” said Senator Mike Lee. “Criminals on the lam can escape to DC after performing abortions in states where they are illegal, because they know DC will let them get away with it. This bill will repeal DC’s safe harbor for illegal abortionists and peddlers of drugs for transexual procedures, restoring the rule of law to Washington.”
statements.context: introducing D.C. Shield Law Repeal Act

statements.text: “ The Federal Government should never fund research that harms kids.  This bill will protect taxpayers from funding spurious research, but more importantly, it will protect kids from the permanent damage this irresponsible research can produce .”
statements.context: introducing Protecting Our Kids from Harmful Research Act (spacing as in source)

statements.text: “Americans are becoming more tolerant every day, which is why the Equality Act is so counterproductive. It unnecessarily pits communities against each other and divides our nation when patience and understanding are so sorely needed.”

statements.text: Children’s first teachers are their parents, and parents must carry the primary responsibility to oversee and direct their children’s education.
